transcript.answer: No. HAL Engine's `resilience` setting is only a retry policy and has no fallback field. HAL Engine fails over only through `fallbackProviders`. Issue #179 / PR #438 validated `FALLBACK_MODEL_ID` against the allowlist and printed it in the `api.model` startup line. `buildEngine` in `apps/api/src/server.ts` passed `createHalEngine` a `provider` but no `fallbackProviders`, so the fallback was never tried. Issue #474 / PR #475 (merged) fixed this. The resolved fallback is now the only entry in `fallbackProviders`, and the list is empty when `FALLBACK_MODEL_ID` is unset. PR #475 also refuses fallbacks the engine cannot serve. For now only the mock row can be a fallback, until a fallback vendor is chosen (KU-07), because a real fallback needs that vendor's own settings. One spec line (User Story 3, scenario 5 of the support-agent-prompt-and-model spec) still describes a `resilience.fallback.provider` block, which is the earlier, mistaken assumption.

judgements.reason: The answer correctly says resilience is only a retry policy and that buildEngine never passed fallbackProviders, but it claims only the mock row can be a fallback, whereas the gold says a mock fallback is refused.
